inventory_summary: Inventoried 40 drain runs (35 DWV, 5 condensate/TPR), 28 vent runs + the VR-M-STACK vent/radon riser, 13 resolved cleanouts, 27 drain fixtures, the three 3" stack walls. Sources: authored in plan/mep_drainage.py, mep_venting.py, mep_vent_tees.py, mep_cleanouts.py; tables in resolve/plumbing_tables.py (Table 1002.2 rows verified against a secondary 2018 UPC printout; MN 4714.1002 amendment read at revisor.mn.gov); pipe sizes in the catalogue (library/fittings.py has no laying lengths). Probes: per-segment slope of every drain; per-fixture arm walk (engine function) plus my own fall and first-leg analysis; vent connectivity in 3D; stack-in-wall plan overlap; cleanout fitting/vent coaxiality; three haus route --fixture feasibility runs. Verified clean: slope, vent grade direction, vent network, stack fit, cleanout access. NOT examined: vent SIZING vs developed length (UPC 904/906 tables) and vent roof-termination geometry beyond the citation; under-slab pipe bedding/cover and the building-sewer exit invert; fitting-body clearances (no laying lengths in the catalogue); cleanout front clearances against real obstacles (only authored clear_width/depth read); storm leaders, sump discharge and site drains (P-201..204 opened, not measured); condensate drains' fixture ends; the supply runs the vent routes collide with (M2 owns supply); engineering/seal impact of any moved pipe; permit-set dimension strings (D1). The PDF sheets A-401.1-.6 and P-101..P-204 were all opened.

findings.title: Nine vents leave their drain horizontally at the drain's centreline height, below the flood rim, instead of rising first; nothing grades it

evidence.measured: Each vent's first vertex is on its drain's centreline (|dz| <= 0.6") and its FIRST segment is level, not vertical: PR-B-BATH-WC-VENT 22.4" level (z -119.2 -> -118.8) before it rises 100"; PR-B-SAUNA-VENT 26.2"; PR-B-SAUNA-FD-VENT 25.3"; PR-M-BATH2-SH-VENT 21.9"; PR-S-BATH1-WC-VENT 17.0"; PR-M-LSINK-VENT 16.0"; PR-M-BATH2-WC-VENT 15.3"; PR-S-SUITEBATH-WC-VENT 14.4" then 2.4" + 28.0" + 1.2" more, all within 2.5" of the closet drain's elevation (z 116.6-118.2, flood rim 150.6); PR-S-BATH1-SH-VENT 9.0". Every one stays more than 6" below its fixture's rim for that leg (rim = fixture body top, the engine's own conservative read). No check reads this: mep.vent_grade grades only drops/sags, mep.trap_arm_developed accepts any vent end within r+1/2" of the drain in 3D (TEE_TOL_M).
evidence.expected: A vent connects ABOVE the centreline of a horizontal drain and rises vertically to 6" over the fixture's flood-level rim before any horizontal leg; a leg under that line is a drainage-fitting, drain-graded pipe (UPC 905.2/905.3: the engine's own routing/trap_vent.py:5 and route_fixture_vent.py:20 apply exactly this rule to every route it proposes, but not to the authored ones). A level leg leaving at the centreline is a side inlet.
evidence.method: Python probe on the pickled resolved model: for each vent run, take the end that lies on a drain (resolve.mep_trap_arm._project within radius+TEE_TOL_M), walk the vent from there, and list the first segments with max z <= rim+6" (rim = model.canvas_objects body_z1_m of the fixture whose drain it tees) and plan length > 0.5"; scripts /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-colincatlin-Documents-NoCloud-TypeHaus/fc951bd3-20bf-434f-9b45-0a1dac7cd982/scratchpad/geometry-review/M5/p4.py and /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-colincatlin-Documents-NoCloud-TypeHaus/fc951bd3-20bf-434f-9b45-0a1dac7cd982/scratchpad/geometry-review/M5/p5.py.

findings.title: mep.trap_arm_developed counts a vertical drop as arm length and never grades the fall against the pipe diameter (the router refuses the same arm as an S-trap)

evidence.measured: Fall from the arm's first vertex (the fixture drain point) to the vent tee the check accepts, non-water-closet fixtures: FX-M-LAUNDRY-SINK 15.2" on a O2" arm (drain point z 0.0, tee z -15.2 at the bottom of the drop); FX-M-BATH2-SH 22.0" (O2"); FX-S-BATH1-SH 19.1" (O1.5"); FX-B-SAUNA-SH 10.3" and FX-B-SAUNA-FD 8.3" (O2"); FX-A-STUBATH-SH 4.8" (O2"). The finding messages call these arms '15"', '22"', '26"', '10"', '8"', '5"', i.e. the drop itself. Water closets (closet-bend drops of 4-22") excluded: the bend is the arm's first leg by practice. The model has no trap, so the weir is not known; the drain point is a floor or stub-out, which makes the true fall at least this large.
evidence.expected: A trap arm may not fall more than one pipe diameter before its vent (otherwise an S-trap, UPC 1002.2 / 1001): the engine's own router enforces it (arm_reach: 'Horizontal edges only (a drop before the vent is an S-trap)') so the check and the router disagree about what a vented arm is; arm_is_vented uses the check's walk, so the router also never offers these fixtures a better vent.
evidence.method: Probe /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-colincatlin-Documents-NoCloud-TypeHaus/fc951bd3-20bf-434f-9b45-0a1dac7cd982/scratchpad/geometry-review/M5/p8.py: for every Fixture, arm_leaves() then developed_arm() (the check's own walk), plus the nearest vent end on any drain (resolve.mep_trap_arm._project); fall = first-vertex z - tee z. Also read routing/trap_vent.py:3-6 and :54.

findings.source: routing/trap_vent.py docstring (S-trap rule, UPC 1002.2 as the engine cites it); MN 4714.1002 as amended is silent on fall (https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/4714.1002/), so the diameter rule is the engine's own reading of the UPC, not verified in the 2018 text.
findings.proposed_fix: Add the router's fall rule to mep.trap_arm_developed (ADVISORY first): arm fall to the tee <= arm diameter, trap weir at the fixture's trap model if one exists. In the house: put the tee at the top of the drop (sanitary tee at the trap-arm stub, vent up, drain down), which also fixes M5-101 for LSINK/BATH2-SH/BATH1-SH.

findings.title: mep.drain_tie_in prints arrival heights of +98.9" to +144.6" 'above the centreline' for ties onto vertical stacks

Cause: pipe_invert_at(parent, end_point) matches in plan only; on a vertical parent segment the plan point is degenerate and returns the segment's low end. Example: PR-B-WC2-DRAIN ends at (36.0, 198.0, -25.5), 0.8" above PR-B-MAIN-DRAIN's stack-top vertex (36.0, 198.0, -26.3), which then falls to -124.4. evidence.expected: 'Arrives X above the pipe's centreline at the junction' for a stack means the height along the stack's own z span, 0.8" here.
evidence.method: Baseline checks.json mep.drain_tie_in messages; PR-B-MAIN-DRAIN path (36,198,-26.3)->(36,198,-124.4) from m.pipe_runs; read mep_tie_ins.py:96-104.

findings.proposed_fix: Return a station on the parent's 3D segment (nearest point to the child's end vertex in 3D) and report the child's z minus the parent's z at that station; for a vertical parent report the arrival as 'on a stack'.
